en: The Sūtra on the Maṇḍala of Samantabhadra Spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīlagupta, Imperially Appointed Court Disperser and Acting Junior Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial,
Dharma-Master Subject Śīlagupta, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying on Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha,
together with a great assembly of bhikṣus numbering five million.
Furthermore, there were great bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who were all fully endowed with every pure dharma (śukla-dharma),
who had attained immeasurable wisdom and skillful means, and were able to roar the lion’s roar.
Their names were:
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ratnamudrāhasta.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Playful,
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Adorned with Merit,
and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sound of Blessed Virtue.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mahāmati,
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Guṇavyūha,
and such a multitude of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas all gathered together.
At that time, the World-Honored One, out of great kindness and great compassion,
for the sake of all practitioners of the present and future who wish to cultivate the secret yoga of Vajrasattva, [spoke as follows].
Regarding "swift accomplishment," the Buddha spoke the Dharma of the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu,
saying: "If there is a son of good family..."
For one who wishes to enter the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu and swiftly achieve accomplishment by practicing the secret method of the union with Samantabhadra-Vajrasattva:
First, one should generate a courageous, firm, and sublime resolve;
then, seek out a pure and excellent master of the world and request the conferral of empowerment.
From that master, receive the oral transmission of the ritual methods for the secret mudrās and their corresponding applications.
Retain each one with focused mindfulness, ensuring there is no error or forgetfulness.
Thereafter, proceed as desired to a pure and excellent location.
One should practice this dharma to seek siddhi.
Having attained a superior state,
one should first bathe to become pure and thoroughly cleanse both body and mind.
Then, at that location, first perform the boundary-binding and protection of the body.
Thereafter, according to the ritual rules, smear the maṇḍala with fragrant mud, ensuring it is perfectly executed according to the dharma.
Having finished smearing it, [one should act] within this maṇḍala.
Incense and flowers are offered in various ways as worship;
one should then perform visualization directed toward this maṇḍala,
visualizing the Tathāgata, the principal deity, within that maṇḍala.
Having attained this presence, one does not rise from the seat;
instead, one takes scented ointment and anoints the hands,
forms the mudrā, and recites the secret mantra.
Next, bind the seal for purifying the three karmas.
With both hands in the vajra-palms gesture, recite the root mantra three times:
*Oṃ svabhāva-śuddhāḥ sarva-dharmāḥ svabhāva-śuddho ’haṃ*. Having recited this mantra, release the seal.
He further says: "From beginningless time until now,
all my coarse and heavy actions of body, speech,
and mind have now been purified."
Having thus become purified,
may all activities now performed serve as the cause for entering that Vajra Dharma.
Then, once again, direct your attention and visualize the Tathāgata as the tutelary deity (iṣṭadevatā).
With the aspiration that all your undertakings may be accomplished, take refuge and offer praise.
Then, recite the secret mantra, saying:
Oṃ sarvatathāgatākāyavākcittapraṇāmavajramanānāṃ karomi. Having recited this secret mantra, [one should proceed].
Thereupon, he prostrated with the fourfold礼 (prostrations) to the Tathāgata, the principal deity within the maṇḍala.
Having prostrated, he knelt for a long time,
joined his palms in the vajra-mudrā, and spoke these words:
I now resolve to attain unsurpassed bodhicitta.
I pray that the Perfectly Awakened One, the Teacher of the Three Times, will compassionately embrace me through skillful means,
so that I may correctly obtain the three types of training precepts.
For the sake of all sentient beings, by means of the adamantine power of firmness,
I shall uphold the Three Jewels to bring benefit and happiness to sentient beings.
Now, within this secret dharma of the Tathāgata’s Vajradhātu, which is in correspondence with the true suchness (*tathatā*) of Vajrasattva—
From the ācārya, one receives the Great Vajra Family;
one practices the four kinds of giving during the six periods of the day.
From the Great Jewel Family, one receives the Dharma of Equal Correspondence.
Within the Great Lotus Family, one receives the subtle and secret Dharma of the three vehicles.
Within the Great Activity Family, one receives the complete array of all ritual activities for making offerings.
From the purity of *tathatā* (suchness), the Dharma of great bodhi arises.
I have resolved upon the unsurpassed mind of enlightenment;
having received these teachings, I shall practice according to the Dharma to bring benefit to all sentient beings.
For all sentient beings who lack a master, he acts as their master;
he causes those not yet liberated to attain liberation,
and he causes those not yet at peace to attain peace.
"May those who have not reached the other shore reach the other shore.
Having made this vow, the practitioner then recites the Vajra-gaze mantra.
One should visualize Maṭha as the sun and moon at the two eyes;
with both hands in vajra-fists, place them at the sides of the waist,
along with the maṇḍala, incense, flowers, and other articles of offering.
Therefore, regarding the gazing with the eyes: to remove impurities and achieve pure vajra-vision, the mantra is:
Oṃ vajranartimaṭa. With both hands in the vajra-bond (*vajrabandha*).
It is able to untie all fetters and afflictions,
purifying all seeds of defilement within the eighth consciousness.
The mantra for the Vajra-bond is:

Oṃ vajra-bandha svāhā. By reciting this mantra while forming this mudrā, one shall attain complete liberation from all bonds of the latent afflictions (*anuśaya*) that have persisted within one's own body since beginningless time.
One should cause all merits to be cultivated until they are perfected.
Next, one should perform the binding mudrā at the heart and then spread the fingers apart.
Furthermore, recite the secret mantra as follows:
Oṃ vajra-manda-traṭ. By means of this mudrā and the recitation of this mantra, the wisdom of the vajra of one's own nature shall be suddenly manifested.
Having struck the vajra bell three times,
one should then visualize that within one's own body,
the syllable *A* appears as a radiant wheel.
Possessing great majestic power,
for this reason all demonic obstacles shall be unable to disturb or confuse them;
furthermore, they shall attain a vajra-like adamantine mind that is non-retrogressive.
One attains all accomplishments.
Next, recite the heart-mantra:
*Ha ha ha ha hūṃ*. Having recited the heart-mantra, [proceed].
One immediately enters the firm wisdom of Vajrasattva and visualizes that all phenomena throughout the entirety of space are entirely equal,
identical to those sixteen sounds.
Next, visualize your own mind as becoming a full moon disc.
Within that moon disc, visualize the syllable KA;
once it appears clearly and distinctly, further visualize another syllable KA outside the moon disc.
Once it has appeared before one, revolving like a star,
one should again visualize the syllable *ka*.
Within the moon-disc of the heart, a vajra-lotus arises.
Furthermore, from the center of this lotus, a lotus-seal (padmamudrā) emerges.
Upon this seal, one should visualize the syllable HAṂ.
Once the syllable has appeared clearly and distinctly, [one should continue].
Furthermore, one contemplates that one’s own body is identical to Vajrasattva—without difference, without distinction, immovable and unshakable.
Then, brandishing the vajra, one speaks these words:
"I shall not change this body now."
Arising from the Vajra-dharma, one becomes Vajrasattva.
Next, one further visualizes oneself as the Great Samayasattva,
and then binds the Vajra-Mahāsamaya-mudrā.
Recite the secret mantra:
Oṃ samayahaṃ mahāsamayahaṃ. Then, with the previously mentioned *samaya*-mudrā, seal the heart, forehead, throat, and crown of the head.
Next, bind the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) of the Bhagavān and recite the mantra:
Oṃ samayasattva ātiṣṭha svāhā. Recite the mantra once more:
Oṃ vajradharma hiri. By means of this mudrā and mantra, may my body, speech, and mind become the three vajra activities.
Next, bind the Great Seal of Accomplishment and recite the mantra:
Oṃ samaya aḥ. Then, visualize within the moon disc at the heart before you the wheel of the syllable Aḥ of Vajradharma and a lotus.
Up to the syllable *haṃ* within the lotus,
each and every one is manifested from within my own Vajradharma-svabhāvakāya (the self-nature body of the Vajra Dharma).
Having formed this perception:
Then, one forms the Vajrāṅkuśa mudrā:
with both hands, form vajra-fists and hook the two little fingers together in a reversed manner.
Bend the two index fingers like hooks and recite the mantra:
Oṃ vajra-kuśa jaḥ. Next, form the Vajrapāśa mudrā.
Without altering the previous mudrā,
one should instead hook the two index fingers with their tips facing inward;
this is called the Pāśa-mudrā (Noose Mudrā).
Then recite the secret mantra:
Oṃ vajrapāśa hūṃ. Next, form the Vajra-Chain mudrā by interlacing the two hands with the palms facing inward.
This is called the Vajra-Chain.
Then recite the mantra:
Oṃ vajrasphoṭa vaṃ. Next, bind the Vajra-Bell mudrā.
With both hands in the vajra-bond,
shake them three times as if ringing a bell;
this is called the vajra-bell.
Then recite the secret mantra:
Oṃ vajra-veśaya. Next, visualize oneself as identical to the wisdom-body of Vajrasattva.
Having seen this before you, [proceed].
Then recite the secret mantra:
JAḤ HŪṂ VAṂ HOḤ. Next, bind the samaya-mudrā and recite the secret mantra:
Having recited this secret mantra— Oṃ samayas tvaṃ—
one then visualizes one's own mind as becoming a full moon disc and imagines oneself entering this moon disc.
One becomes the Great Vajrasattva.
Then, one recites the mantra:
Oṃ mahāsamayasatvaḥ. Next, one recites the Vajradharma mantra:
Having recited this secret mantra— Oṃ vajradharma hrīḥ—
one should again visualize that the preceding moon disc of the mind transforms into a red color.
Within it is the principal deity, a Tathāgata of extraordinary and sublime marks and signs;
his eyes are like lotus petals, and he wears a smiling countenance.
Out of compassion and joy, he dwells in a state of serene composure.
Having observed in this manner,
one next binds the secret mudrās of the samaya of the four Tathāgatas,
consecrating the body with each of their respective root mantras.
First, bind the Vajrasattva mudrā:
with both hands form the vajra-bind,
and extend the two middle fingers upright like needles.
This is called the Vajrasattva Mudrā.
Placing this mudrā at the heart,
one recites the mantra as follows:
Oṃ sarvavajri adhiṣṭhasva svāhā. Without altering the previous mudrā, [recite this].
Bend the two middle fingers so they resemble a jewel;
this is called the Vajraratna.
This mudrā is to be placed upon the forehead.
Then recite the secret mantra:
Oṃ ratnavajri adhiṣṭhāya svāhā. Do not alter the previous mudrā.
With the two middle fingers joined like lotus petals,
it is called the Vajrapadma mudrā.
This mudrā is placed at the throat.
Then recite the secret mantra:
Oṃ dharmavajri adhiṣṭhāya svāha. Without altering the previous mudrā, [continue].
Interlace the two middle fingers and extend them upward;
this is called the Karma-mudrā.
Place this mudrā upon the crown of the head.
Then he recites the secret mantra:
Oṃ karmavajri adhiṣṭhasva svāhā. Next, he again visualizes the Tathāgata, the Principal Deity, within the previously mentioned red lunar disc.
Then, perform the mudrā for summoning by snapping the fingers:
cross the arms and make the vajra finger-snap.
This same procedure applies equally to the invocation of all Buddhas.
If one snaps the fingers with the left hand, all virtuous undertakings will be swiftly accomplished.
If one snaps the fingers with the right hand, a swift assembly will be gathered.
The mantra for snapping the fingers is as follows:
Oṃ vajrasamāja jaḥ. Then recite the one hundred and eight names, which say:
Homage to the Great Being born from the Vajra, To all the Vajra Tathāgatas, To Samantabhadra of the Vajrayāna, And to Vajrapāṇi.
Vajrarāja, Wondrous Enlightenment;
Vajrāṅkuśa, Tathāgata, Firm and Unfailing King;
I prostrate to Vajradaṇḍa, Vajrarāga, Great Bliss; Vajraśara, Subduer.
Vajra Great Māra-Desire, I prostrate to the Vajra Bow;
Vajra Mind, Wondrous Peak, I prostrate to the Vajra Silence, Great Love;
Vajra Joy, King of Rapture, I prostrate to you.
Vajra-ratna-suvikrānta, Vajra-śūnyatā-mahāratna,
Vajra-gaganagañja; I prostrate to Vajragarbha,
Vajra-tejo-mahājvāla, and Vajraprabha-Buddhasūrya.
Homage to the Great Illumination of Vajra Flames;
Homage to the Vajra Banner of Sublime Benefit;
To the Vajra Flag of Wondrous Joy and the Vajra Great Jewel Banner, The Firm and Stable Summit, I prostrate.
Vajra Laughter, Great Joy; Vajra Thought, Greatly Wondrous;
Vajra Love, Delightful; Vajra Love, Prostrated To;
Vajradharma, Sublime Benefit; Vajrapadma, Sublime Purity.
Homage to the Vajra Eye, the Sovereign of the Sublime Eye;
Homage to the Vajra Sharpness, the Great Vehicle;
Homage to the Vajra Hook, the Great Diadem, the Profound Mañjuśrī; Homage to the Vajra Wisdom.
Vajra-Cause Great Realm, Vajra-Wheel Mahāyāna,
Vajra-Supreme Wisdom Turning, I prostrate to the Vajra-Realm,
the Wondrously Luminous Vajra-Speech, The Wondrous Accomplishment of Vajra-Mindfulness.
Vajra Accomplishment, the Wordless; I prostrate to the Vajra Speech, the Supreme Wisdom;
To all Vajra Activities, the Great Power of Vajra Emptiness; I prostrate to the Vajra Action.
Vajrapāla of great valor, Vajrakaṅkaṭa of great firmness,
wrathful and wondrously courageous; I prostrate to Dṛḍhavīrya,
the firm-eater of great skill, Vajradaṃṣṭra of great terror.
Vajra Peak Destroyer of Māras, firm in majestic wrath,
I prostrate to Vajramuṣṭi of wondrous intent; Vajrabandha, liberation,
Vajramuṣṭi of equanimity, firm fist, I prostrate to you.
By reciting these one hundred and eight supreme names,
one obtains all the foremost empowerments.
Should anyone be able to honor and praise these names, [they shall attain such results].
Because one upholds the Great Vajra,
if one constantly chants and recites these names and phrases,
one shall obtain the renown of a Vajradhara.
Therefore, I have already previously explained the visualization.
Once the deity, the Tathāgata, has been perceived before one,
one should immediately perform the rite of summoning by forming the Vajrāṅkuśa mudrā, the seal of activity.
Once [the deity] has descended,
one should immediately form the samaya-mudrā and again recite the secret mantra, saying:
Oṃ vajradharma jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ samayas tvaṃ mā haṃ. Then, recite the mantra of the Vajra Dharma:
Oṃ vajradharma hīḥ. Next, join the two index fingers together and bend them like lotus petals.
This is called the Vajradharma Samaya-mudrā.
Next is the Great Karma-mudrā, the World-Honored One’s Great Seal, followed by the Consecration Seal.
Then, having presented the five offerings:
Then, recite the secret mantra that one has previously practiced until the count is complete; having done so,
form the mudrā and recite the mantra of the eight offerings.
To make offerings to the Buddhas, noble ones,
and so forth, one should form the vajra-fist mudrā with both hands,
place them at the sides of the waist, and slightly lower the head to the left.
This is called the Playful Gesture (līlāmudrā). Then, recite the mantra:
Oṃ vajrarase. Next, form the vajra-fists with both hands.
Pointing both index fingers toward the forehead and the back of the head as if tying a garland—
this is called the Garland Mudrā (Mālāmudrā).
Then he recited the secret mantra:
*Oṃ vajramāle*. Next, with both hands joined in the *vajrapāṇi* (diamond-hand) gesture, he spread the five fingers apart as if holding flowers.
This is called the Gāyatrī Seal.
Then recite the mantra:
Oṃ vajragīte. Next, form the vajra-fists with both hands.
First, join the palms with an open mind, then perform the movement as in a dance.
This is called the Dance Mudrā (Nṛtya-mudrā).
Then recite the secret mantra:
Oṃ vajranṛtye. Next, form the vajrabandha with both hands and then release them downward;
this is called the incense-offering mudrā.
Then, recite the secret mantra:
Oṃ vajra-dhūpe. Next, form the inner vajra-bind with the eight fingers;
hold them open before the heart in the manner of offering a flower.
This is called the Flower Offering Mudrā.
Then recite the mantra:
Oṃ vajrapuṣpe. Next, form the Vajrabandha with both hands.
Extending both index fingers constitutes the *dīpāhuti-mudrā* (lamp-offering mudrā).
Then, recite the mantra:
Oṃ Vajra-roki. Next, form the *vajrabandha* with both hands.
One should apply [the ointment] upon one's own heart;
this is the mudrā for offering scented unguent.
Then, recite the secret mantra as follows:
Oṃ vajra-ghaṇṭe. These various secret mantras and mudrās possess great power;
one must apply the mind to benefit both oneself and others.
Furthermore, abiding oneself in the samaya-concordance,
one visualizes the wheel of the syllable Oṃ appearing within the heart.
Once the appearance of the syllable has been attained:
Furthermore, visualize that from within the syllable Oṃ,
there flow forth precious canopies, jeweled banners, precious pennants, bracelets, earrings, necklaces, garments, crowns, and other such precious ornaments;
even clouds of food and drink of a hundred flavors and the seven precious gems.
Directing the mind one by one,
offer with reverent devotion before each Buddha and Bodhisattva to extend worship.
Then, perform the Vajra-joined-palms mudrā.
Distribute the visualization by offering it to all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and others of the ten directions.
Having performed such offerings,
one should then dedicate the merit of the recitation or whatever virtuous deeds have been performed, and make aspiration prayers.
Then, according to the ritual, he dispatched and respectfully sent off the worthy sages.
At that time, after the World-Honored One had spoken this Dharma,
the great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas present in the assembly—
Together with the entire great assembly of bhikṣus,
having heard what the Buddha had spoken, they rejoiced, accepted it with faith, prostrated to the Buddha, and withdrew.
Thus concludes the *Buddhabhāṣita Samantabhadramaṇḍala Sūtra*.
